title: Multi-Cloud Audit Feed Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `matching activity` into `index=cloud_multi`. Confirm UC-4.4.33 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `matching activity`. Confirm UC-4.4.33 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud_multi` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.33_multi_cloud_audit_feed_h_33"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.33 — Multi-Cloud Audit Feed Health: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for configured audit predicates and returns actor, resource, and region context for audit review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Multi-Cloud Audit Feed Health' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.33 drives critical-priority audit alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable aws:cloudtrail ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=cloud_multi.
visualization: Ingestion health single value and lag chart.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud_multi`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): none.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable aws:cloudtrail ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=cloud_multi.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud_multi sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.33_multi_cloud_audit_feed_h_33"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=cloud_multi` to detect multi-cloud audit feed health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_33_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Ingestion health single value and lag chart..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud audit feed health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
